1Outcome

Each participant accessing a specialist disability accommodation dwelling is able to exercise choice and control and is supported by effective tenancy management.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Demonstrated adherence to the requirements established in the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rules 2018.

Our commitment: Policy C1, Policy C2, Policy C3, Policy C5. Proof: Register col B, Register col P, Register col Q, Register col R, Register col S, Register col T, Register col U, Register col AB, Register col AJ, Register col AK, Register col BD.

(2)

Where applicable, policies and procedures are in place about how a provider will declare, advertise and fill vacancies in shared living, including how each participant’s views, preferences and needs are documented and taken into account. The policies are made available to participants in the language, mode of communication and terms which each participant is most likely to understand.

Our commitment: Policy C3, Policy C4. Proof: Register col I, Register col V, Register col AI, Register col AK, Register col AL, Register col AM, Register col AN, Register col AO, Register col AP, Register col AQ, Register col AR, Register col AS, Register col AT.

(3)

Documented arrangements are in place with each participant and each participant’s other NDIS providers that deliver supported independent living supports within a specialist disability accommodation dwelling. At a minimum, the arrangements should outline the party or parties responsible and their roles (where applicable) for the following matters:

  1. (a)How the specialist disability accommodation provider will work with other providers who deliver supported independent living supports to ensure the shared living arrangement is working for all tenants;
  2. (b)How potential conflicts involving the participant will be managed;
  3. (c)Policies and procedures for responding to violence, abuse, exploitation or conflict involving one or more participant which may impact on the condition of the dwelling;
  4. (d)How each participant’s concerns about the specialist disability accommodation dwelling will be communicated to and addressed by the specialist disability accommodation provider;
  5. (e)How behaviours of concern will be managed, if this a relevant issue for the participant;
  6. (f)How changes to a participant’s circumstances or supports will be agreed and communicated;
  7. (g)Arrangements for continuity of supports (including specialist disability accommodation) in the event or a natural disaster or other emergency; and
  8. (h)In shared living, how vacancies will be filled including the participant’s right to have their needs, wishes, choices and situation taken into account.

Our commitment: Policy C5. Proof: Register col H, Register col I, Register col X, Register col Y, Register col Z, Register col AA, Register col AC, Register col AD, Register col AH.

(4)

Allegations and incidents of violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination, are acted upon, each participant affected is supported and assisted, records are made of any details and outcomes of reviews and investigations (where applicable), and action is taken to prevent similar incidents occurring in the future.

Our commitment: Policy C7, Policy C14. Proof: Register col O, Register col BI, Register col BJ, Register col BL, Register col BM.

(5)

Where a change in participant needs or circumstances occurs, reasonable adjustments are made to accommodate the changes. If the changed support needs exceed the design category or functionality of the dwelling, work is undertaken to modify the dwelling, following consideration of the impact of the modifications on the other tenants (if applicable). Where the participant’s needs or circumstances cannot be accommodated, the participant, and any relevant support providers are made aware of the need to find alternative accommodation.

Our commitment: Policy C10, Policy C11. Proof: Register col W, Register col BC, Register col BF, Register col BG, Register col BH.

(6)

A complaints management and resolution system is maintained that meets the requirements of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018 and follows the principles of procedural fairness and natural justice.

Our commitment: Policy C14. Proof: Register col O, Register col AS, Register col AX, Register col AY, Register col BB.

(7)

An incident management system is maintained in accordance with the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.

Our commitment: Policy C14. Proof: Register col O, Register col BL.

(8)

State or territory legislative requirements regarding the provision of tenancy-related notices are adhered to and each participant is aware of their right to seek review of a decision, where applicable.

Our commitment: Policy C2, Policy C13. Proof: Register col S, Register col U, Register col W, Register col AU, Register col AV, Register col AW, Register col AX, Register col AY, Register col AZ, Register col BB, Register col BC, Register col BE.

(9)

Policies, procedures and agreements relating to any tenancy management are provided in the language, mode of communication and terms which each participant is most likely to understand.

Our commitment: Policy C4. Proof: Register col H, Register col I, Register col R, Register col V, Register col AC, Register col AD, Register col AM, Register col AR, Register col BA.

1Purpose

This policy sets out how [Provider name] manages the tenancy of each participant in its specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwellings. Its aim is that each participant can exercise choice and control over their home. It is for participants, their supporters, their supported independent living (SIL) providers, our workers and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and every participant who lives in one.
  • Every vacancy, and change in a participant's needs in those dwellings.
  • Every with a participant's .
  • Every worker who manages, maintains or visits a dwelling for us: employees, contractors, agents and volunteers.
  • Every complaint and incident that a tenancy.

Where [Provider name] also delivers SIL in a dwelling, this policy applies to us as the . POL-SIL-05 Agreements about Tenancy, Housing and Support Arrangements Policy applies to us as the SIL provider. This policy does not cover the supports a SIL provider delivers. Each SIL provider answers for those under its own policies.

3Commitments

C1

We will house a participant only in a dwelling that is enrolled, and never above the number of it is enrolled for. We start SDA only when the written service agreement is signed. We may also start when a proposed copy has been given and explained, and we provide SDA on its terms.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 5, Procedure step 11.

C2

We will follow the landlord, tenancy, building, and health and safety law that applies to each dwelling. We make sure everyone we employ or engage does the same. We keep the state or territory rules for tenancy notices in the register, built from the one dated list of laws in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register, and check each one against the law at least every 12 months and whenever the law changes.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (8). How we do it: Procedure step 19, Procedure step 24, Procedure step 29.

C3

We will declare, advertise and fill every vacancy in the same fair way. We tell the NDIA in writing within 5 . We advertise in at least 2 places for at least 10 business days. We ask each current resident before any offer, and we choose only on criteria we publish.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (2), Legislation (3)(h). How we do it: Procedure step 1, Procedure step 2, Procedure step 3, Procedure step 4, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 6, Procedure step 7, Procedure step 8, Procedure step 9, Procedure step 10, Procedure step 11.

C4

We will give each participant our vacancy process, their tenancy agreements and every tenancy notice. We use the language, mode of communication and terms which that participant is most likely to understand. We write down what they said back.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (9). How we do it: Procedure step 9, Procedure step 12, Procedure step 26, Procedure step 27.

C5

We will agree a documented arrangement with each participant and each of their SIL providers. It names, for each matter, the party responsible, their role, a contact person and a response time. Where a participant does not agree or sign, we record it in their words, and nothing changes in their tenancy.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (3), Legislation (3)(a). How we do it: Procedure step 12, Procedure step 13, Procedure step 14.

C6

We will help residents settle early and fairly. We meet each person affected, alone, within 5 business days. We never move a person, or limit their access, to settle a conflict.

Answers: Legislation (3)(b). How we do it: Procedure step 16.

C7

We will act on every allegation or incident of violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination in or around a dwelling. We act on the day we learn of it. We support each person affected, record the details and the outcome of every review, and change something to stop a repeat. The person harmed keeps their home.

Answers: Legislation (3)(c), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 17, Procedure step 18, Procedure step 19.

C8

We will take every concern about a dwelling from anyone, and acknowledge it within 1 business day. We record each concern, even one that is not a complaint or a repair. We give an answer, or a date for one, within 5 business days. We make an emergency safety problem safe the same day and an urgent one within 24 hours.

Answers: Legislation (3)(d). How we do it: Procedure step 15.

C9

We will manage that may put a tenancy at risk through the participant's supports, not through the tenancy. We take no tenancy action about behaviour until we have asked the participant and offered an advocate. We also ask their SIL provider and behaviour support practitioner, with their agreement, what would help.

Answers: Legislation (3)(e). How we do it: Procedure step 20.

C10

We will agree each change in a participant's needs or circumstances with them first. We pass it on, within 2 business days, only to the people they choose. We make , and we modify the dwelling where the new needs call for it, after asking each other resident affected.

Answers: Legislation (3)(f), Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 22.

C11

We will tell a participant in person, within 2 business days of confirming it, when their home cannot meet their needs. We tell the providers they choose and help them find another home. The participant decides whether and when to move. We do not serve a notice on that ground until the Chief Executive has reviewed every other option with them and an advocate.

Answers: Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 23, Procedure step 28.

C12

We will agree with each participant and each SIL provider how supports and accommodation continue in an emergency or a disaster. We give each SIL provider the dwelling's safety and emergency information before its first shift, and we keep the safety features tested. If the dwelling cannot be used, we arrange, with the participant's SIL provider and their emergency plan, safe temporary accommodation as soon as possible and within 24 hours, and a place that meets their access and equipment needs as soon as one can be found. We pay for or help fund it where the law or the agreement puts that on us.

Answers: Legislation (3)(g). How we do it: Procedure step 14, Procedure step 21.

C13

We will give every tenancy notice as the law of the state or territory requires: on a ground the law allows, in the form the law prescribes, with every prerequisite notice and third-party notification the law requires. A notice to vacate gives at least 90 days, and never because of the participant's choice of SIL provider, a complaint, or a refusal to sign an arrangement. A rent change gives the longer of what the law requires and 60 days. The Chief Executive approves each notice that would end a tenancy. We hear the participant first before any notice that would end or limit their tenancy. With every notice we tell them how to seek a review.

Answers: Legislation (8). How we do it: Procedure step 24, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 26, Procedure step 27, Procedure step 28.

C14

We will deal with every complaint and every incident about a tenancy through our complaints system and our incident system. Both meet the NDIS rules, and both treat each person fairly.

Answers: Legislation (4), Legislation (6), Legislation (7). How we do it: Procedure step 15, Procedure step 18, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 29, Procedure step 30.

4Ground rules

G1

A dwelling is the participant's home first. Their tenancy rights come before our convenience and before any funding deadline.

G2

A participant's tenancy never depends on their choices about supports. Changing SIL provider, not signing an arrangement, making a complaint and taking a risk they chose are never grounds for a notice. A notice for any of these reasons is and an incident.

G3

Every adult is presumed able to decide for themselves. A family member or advocate is not a decision maker unless an order or instrument says so. POL-RGT-03 Independence and Informed Choice Policy applies.

G4

We share a participant's personal information only as they agreed, as the law requires, or to prevent serious harm. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy applies. We write no applicant's name in our registers.

G5

This policy authorises no . A limit on a participant's access, belongings, visitors or movement exists only in an authorised behaviour support plan.

G6

The person harmed keeps their home. A move is the participant's choice. Nobody is moved for raising a concern, or for being easier to move than another person.

G7

No resident is asked to accept a housemate to fill a place quickly. A funding deadline is ours to manage, not theirs.

G8

We offer no gift, discount or reward to attract an applicant.

G9

Where the law of the state or territory gives a participant a longer notice or a stronger right than this policy, the law applies.

G10

A person a concern or complaint is about never manages, assesses or approves it.

G11

A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. A statutory time limit is never extended.

G12

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds them all. Where this policy asks for a second person, the sole trader asks the independent contact for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A provider with no governing body sends the quarterly report to that contact.

SDA provider
the registered NDIS provider that owns or manages an enrolled dwelling and houses participants in it.
SIL provider
any other NDIS provider that delivers supported independent living supports to a participant in the dwelling.
enrolled dwelling
a dwelling the NDIA has enrolled to provide SDA, for a set number of residents.
resident
a person who lives in the dwelling, whether or not they use our services.
arrangement
the written agreement between a participant, the SDA provider and each SIL provider that names who is responsible for each matter.
tenancy notice
any notice about a participant's tenancy that the law of the state or territory regulates. Examples are an entry notice, a rent change and a notice to vacate.
conflict
a disagreement between people who live in the home. It is not a conflict of interest.
behaviours of concern
behaviour that puts the person or others at risk, or may put their tenancy at risk.
restrictive practice
anything that limits a person's rights or freedom of movement. Five kinds are regulated: seclusion, and chemical, mechanical, physical and environmental restraint.
reasonable adjustment
a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate. It lets a participant use their home on the same terms as anyone else.
modification
a change to the building, or to something fixed to it.
payback
treating a person worse for raising a concern, making a complaint or using a right.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
concern
anything a participant, a resident, a supporter, a worker or another provider raises about a dwelling that is not yet a complaint, a repair or an incident. Each one gets a concern row in REG-SDA-02.

1Purpose

The result: each participant who lives in one of our specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwellings has a lawful, fair tenancy that they understand. A vacancy is filled with each 's say. The participant's supported independent living (SIL) providers have agreed in writing who does what. A is served only as the law allows, and the participant knows they can ask for a review.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation), C1 to C14.

the : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

2When and who

Use this procedure for every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and for every participant who lives in one.

It starts at six points:

  • a place becomes free, or is about to (steps 1 to 11)
  • a participant moves in, a starts or changes, or an is due for review (steps 12 to 14)
  • day to day: a , a , harm, a behaviour that may put a tenancy at risk, or an emergency (steps 15 to 21)
  • a participant's needs or circumstances change (steps 22 and 23)
  • we need to give a tenancy notice, or a tenancy ends (steps 24 to 28)
  • the register is due for review (steps 29 and 30).

A participant who already lives in a dwelling when you adopt this procedure starts at step 12.

Who acts:

  • The does the day-to-day tenancy work: advertising, applicants, residents, agreements, notices and records.
  • The decides who is offered a place, takes charge of every response to harm, and owns the register.
  • The Chief Executive reviews every notice that would end a tenancy and every decision that a home cannot meet a participant's needs.
  • The Quality Manager samples the register and reports to the governing body.
  • Every worker who sees, hears or is told of harm, a concern or a conflict passes it on. Workers include employees, contractors, agents and volunteers.
  • Each SIL provider acts as the arrangement says.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds them all. Where this procedure asks for a second person, the sole trader asks the independent contact for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

If [Provider name] also delivers SIL in the dwelling, we are both parties at step 12. Two different people sign. PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) also applies.

In this procedure:

  • A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
  • "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020.
  • "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
  • The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

3Before you start

  • Each dwelling is enrolled. It has a row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register with its design category, its building type and the number of residents it is enrolled for.
  • You can open each participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form. If it is more than 12 months old, update it with the participant before anything else.
  • You know whether each participant has agreed to share their information, and with whom. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form shows it.
  • In REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register, each kind of notice in [state or territory] has a notice rule row built from the dated list of laws in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. Each row was checked in the last 12 months and since the law last changed. If one is missing or old, do step 24 first.
  • You hold the urgent line number [urgent line number], the NDIA contact for SDA notices [NDIA contact], and the independent contact for concerns.
  • You hold STA-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancies: Plain Summary, AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement and a blank AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement.

4Watch out

  • Call 000 first if anyone is hurt, in danger or threatened with a weapon. A delay can cost a life.
  • A late notice to the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can then cancel the dwelling's enrolment. It must first give at least 14 days to put it right (SDA Rules 2020, sections 27 and 29).
  • A tenancy never depends on a support choice. A notice given because a participant changed SIL provider, refused to sign an arrangement, complained or took a risk they chose is . It ends a home for the wrong reason.
  • A notice that breaks the state rule may be invalid. The participant is then unsure whether they must leave. We may also face a tribunal.
  • Locking, blocking access, taking belongings or limiting visitors is a . The Restrictive Practices Rules, section 6(e), call it environmental restraint. Without authorisation it can be a reportable incident.
  • Private details about an applicant told to a resident, or the reverse, breach privacy. Share only what each person agreed to.
  • A resident who feels unsafe cannot be talked round. Pushing a housemate on them can hurt them and ends their trust in us.
  • The person harmed keeps their home. Moving or limiting the person who was hurt punishes them for another person's act.
  • A concern about a manager can be buried if it goes only to that manager. Step 17 and If it goes wrong give another line.

5Steps

Fill a vacancy

Step 1

The Tenancy Officer

If a place in an becomes free, or will become free:

Declare the vacancy.

A place becomes free when a participant gives notice, is given notice, dies or moves out. Open a vacancy row. Write the date it arose, the dwelling, the room and the reason. Look up the dwelling in REG-SDA-01. Write its design category, its building type, the number of residents it is enrolled for and the number living there now. Tell the SDA Manager the same day. If a death caused the vacancy, read If it goes wrong first.

Result
The vacancy is on the record and the SDA Manager knows.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AI
Time limit
Within 1 business day of learning of it (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AI.

Step 2

Warning. A late notice breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can then cancel the dwelling's enrolment.

The SDA Manager

If a vacancy arises, a participant gives notice or is given notice to vacate, we propose rent above the limit, or an emergency may make the dwelling unsuitable for SDA:

Notify the NDIA in writing.

Use the channel the NDIA currently asks to use. Write the dwelling, the event, the date it happened and, for a vacancy, that it is available to be filled. Keep a copy and the NDIA's reference. For rent above the limit, attach a certificate from a qualified property valuer that the rent is fair and reasonable. Work out the funding limit date for a dwelling enrolled for 2 to 5 residents. It applies when a participant dies, gives notice, or is given notice because of behaviour that might be a risk. The Rules then treat the participant as still living there until the vacancy is filled. That ends 60 days after the event for 2 or 3 residents, and 90 days for 4 or 5. Write that date. The NDIA decides how it affects payments. This step owns events (e) to (g) of Decision table 6 in PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure, and uses that table for what to send. Events (a) to (d), such as a change of design category, belong to PRO-SDA-01 step 25. We aim to notify within 3 business days; the limit is 5.

Result
The NDIA has been told in writing, inside the limit, and the funding limit date is on the record.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AJ; REG-SDA-02 col AK; REG-SDA-02 col BD; REG-SDA-02 col T; REG-SDA-02 col BN
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the event (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AJ, Register col AK, Register col BD, Register col T, Register col BN.

Step 3

Warning. A vacancy shown only to people we already know shuts out people with the same need.

The Tenancy Officer

Advertise the vacancy.

Post a vacancy notice in at least 2 places that participants and support coordinators use. One must be open to the public without a login. Keep it open for at least 10 business days. State the suburb, the design category, the building type and the rooms. State the number of residents, with no personal detail. State the rent the participant would pay, how we choose using Decision table 1, the closing date, and how to ask for help to apply. Offer the notice in plain language, and in another format on request. Send it to each person on our list who may fit, and to each support coordinator who asked to hear of vacancies. Do not offer a gift, discount or reward to attract an applicant. While the notice is open, book the pre-move-in inspection, or the "vacant room and shared areas" check where the last full inspection is under 6 months old, under PRO-SDA-01 step 19, and ask each resident what matters to them in a housemate so steps 5 and 6 can run as applications arrive. Our target from step 1 to move-in is 30 business days, inside the 60-day funding limit. Law changing: from 20 November 2026 the NDIS Act 2013 bans inducements to provide supports (new section 73VA).

Result
Anyone who may fit can find the vacancy, in a form they can read, and knows how we choose.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AL
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 1 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AL.

Step 4

The Tenancy Officer

Help each applicant to apply.

Take an application in any form: phone, email, letter, in person or through a supporter. Give each applicant a number. Do not write their name in the register. Ask how they want us to communicate. Offer help to apply and an independent advocate. Say how long the process takes, how we choose and when they will hear. Ask only what the criteria need. Get their consent on FRM-INF-01 before you ask anyone else about them.

Result
Every applicant has applied in a way they can, and knows how we choose and when they will hear.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AM
Time limit
Acknowledge each application within 2 business days (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AM.

Step 5

The SDA Manager

Check each applicant against Decision table 1.

Read the part of the applicant's plan that says they are eligible for SDA. Check the design category and building type in it fit this dwelling. Check the applicant will have a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share. Count everyone who will live in the dwelling after the move. The count must not exceed the number it is enrolled for. Ask the applicant about their needs and wishes. With their consent, ask their support coordinator or SIL provider. Write the result for each criterion. Check for a conflict of interest of ours. Examples are a family or business tie, or a link between the vacancy and the applicant's choice of SIL provider. Declare it under PRO-SDA-03. Shortlist the applicants who meet criteria 1 and 2.

Result
Each applicant is checked on the same criteria and the SDA Manager has a shortlist.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AN
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the closing date (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1, Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AN.

Step 6

Warning. A resident who is pushed to accept a housemate may stop raising concerns.

The Tenancy Officer

If the dwelling has other residents:

Ask each resident how they feel about a new person moving in.

Ask before any offer. Ask about the criteria while the vacancy is advertised (step 3) and about the shortlist here, so the two conversations run inside the advertising period. Ask each resident alone, in their own way of communicating, with a supporter or advocate if they want one. Say a place is free and a person may move in. Tell them only what the shortlisted applicants agreed to share. Ask what matters to them in a housemate and what they would like to know. Ask whether they want to meet the person and whether they have any worry. Say that their answer will be heard and never affects their tenancy. For a resident who does not use words, watch and ask a supporter who knows them. The SIL provider may already hold FRM-SIL-06 Co-Tenant Consultation and Matching Record for this vacancy. If so, ask for it with the resident's consent. Do not ask the same questions twice. Write each answer in a few words, without names. Use Decision table 2.

Result
Every resident has been heard before anyone is offered the place.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AO
Time limit
Give each resident at least 5 business days to answer, unless they answer sooner (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AO.

Step 7

The SDA Manager

If a resident says they are worried, do not feel safe, or do not want the person:

Meet the resident to find a way through.

Meet them alone, with an independent advocate or supporter if they want one. Ask what would make it work, such as meeting the person first or a trial visit. Use Decision table 2. Tell them nothing private about the applicant. Do not press them to agree. If they say they do not feel safe, do not offer the place to that applicant until they say the worry is settled. If it is not settled, offer the place to the next applicant and ask each resident again. Sometimes the worry is about who the applicant is, not how they would live together. Explain that we cannot refuse an applicant for that reason. Ask what worries them in daily life.

Result
Each worry has been heard and worked through, and nobody is pushed into a housemate they feel unsafe with.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AP
Time limit
Meet within 2 business days of the resident's answer (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AP.

Step 8

The SDA Manager

Decide which applicant to offer the place to.

Use only the criteria in Decision table 1 and what each resident said. Choose between applicants who meet criteria 1 and 2 by the applicant's own wishes and the residents' views. Use the date they applied only to separate applicants who are equal. Write the reasons against each criterion, in plain words an applicant could test. If no applicant meets criteria 1 and 2, or a resident's safety worry is unresolved for every applicant, offer the place to nobody. Keep the vacancy open and go back to step 3. If the SDA Manager has a conflict of interest, the Chief Executive decides.

Result
The place is offered on stated reasons, with every resident's view taken into account.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AQ
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the last resident's answer (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AQ.

Step 9

The Tenancy Officer

Offer the place to the chosen applicant.

Offer in the applicant's way of communicating. Give them time to decide. Offer a visit to the dwelling, and a meeting with any resident who agrees. Give them the draft SDA service agreement (AGR-SDA-01), the rent they would pay, a draft AGR-SDA-02 and STA-SDA-02. Go through each in their way. Ask them to say back what it means. Offer an independent advocate and independent advice about the agreement. Say that the offer never depends on who delivers their other supports. Say that they can ask for this process in any format. If they decline, say that it counts for nothing against them. Then go back to step 8 and offer the place to the next applicant.

Result
The applicant chooses freely, with what they need to know in a form they understand.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AR
Time limit
At least 5 business days to decide, and longer if they ask (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3, Policy C4. Recorded in: Register col AR.

Step 10

The Tenancy Officer

Tell each applicant who was not offered the place.

Say the result, and the reasons against each criterion, in plain words and in their way. Share nothing about any other applicant or resident. Tell them how to ask the Chief Executive for another look and how to complain to us. Give them the NDIS Commission's number, 1800 035 544. Offer an advocate. Keep them on our list for the next vacancy if they agree.

Result
Each applicant knows why, and how to challenge the decision.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AS
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the chosen applicant's answer (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col AS.

Step 11

The SDA Manager

Confirm the move-in checks.

Obtain the limits check row number from PRO-SDA-01 step 16, dated within 30 days. It shows the dwelling is enrolled, the numbers and the density limit are met, and the room, bathroom and plan fit. Do not confirm the move-in without it. Check that the SDA service agreement is signed. If not, check that a proposed copy was given and explained, and that we will provide SDA on its terms. Check the participant has a copy, or write why not. Check the rent is no more than the NDIS amount plus the participant's reasonable rent contribution. If it is more, go to step 2. Write the bond: the amount, who holds it, and the receipt given. Tell each resident who agreed the move-in date. Tell each SIL provider the participant has chosen, with their consent. Make sure step 12 is booked and step 14 is ready. Open the tenancy row from AGR-SDA-01. Copy what you gave the applicant at step 9 into column V. Write the planned move-in date, and correct it on the day.

Result
The participant moves into a lawful, ready home, and the tenancy is on the record.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col P (the limits check row number and date); REG-SDA-02 col Q; REG-SDA-02 col R; REG-SDA-02 col S; REG-SDA-02 col T; REG-SDA-02 col U; REG-SDA-02 col V; REG-SDA-02 col AT
Time limit
Before the move-in day (statutory for the agreement: SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1); statutory for the limits check: SDA Conditions Rule, section 11(a), and SDA Rules 2020, section 31; our standard for the other checks)

Carries out: Policy C1, Policy C3. Recorded in: Register col P, Register col Q, Register col R, Register col S, Register col T, Register col U, Register col V, Register col AT.

Agree the arrangements with the SIL providers

Step 12

The Tenancy Officer

If a participant moves in, a SIL provider starts or changes, an arrangement changes, no arrangement exists, or 12 months have passed since the last review:

Agree or review the arrangements.

Open an arrangement row. If no SIL provider supports the participant in the dwelling, write "none in this dwelling" and a date within 6 months to check again. Then stop. Otherwise start with the participant alone, with a supporter or advocate if they want one. Go through STA-SDA-02 and each Term of AGR-SDA-02 in their way. Explain that it is separate from their other agreements and that they keep their home whatever they decide. Offer independent advice. Write how you explained it, who was there and what they said back. Complete Sections A and B with them. Then take the same draft to each SIL provider. Check on the NDIS Provider Register that it is registered for SIL. If it is not registered, still make the arrangement (SDA Conditions Rule, section 10(2)(a)), tell the participant plainly, and tell the Chief Executive, who decides whether to notify the NDIS Commission. Settle each matter with a party responsible, a role, a contact and a response time. At a review, ask the participant first what works and what does not, and change only what they want changed. For a participant who already lives there, also write what you gave them in column V.

Result
Every matter has a party responsible, a role, a contact and a response time, and the participant understands what was agreed.
Record
AGR-SDA-02 Q1; REG-SDA-02 col X; REG-SDA-02 col AA; REG-SDA-02 col AC; REG-SDA-02 col V
Time limit
Before move-in where the SIL provider is known. Otherwise within 10 business days of learning who it is. Reviewed at least every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4, Policy C5. Recorded in: Register col X, Register col AA, Register col AC, Register col V.

Step 13

The Tenancy Officer

Record each party's decision about the arrangement.

Give the participant the draft at least 5 business days before you ask for a decision. Ask each party to sign or to give its decision: agrees, agrees in part, does not agree, chose not to sign, or could not sign. A decision given aloud counts. Write who heard it and when. Write the participant's decision in their own words. If they do not agree or sign, write why, what stays in place and when you will offer again. After two refusals, record the participant's standing answer and ask again only at the 12-month review, or when the participant, the SIL provider or their needs change. Nothing changes in their tenancy or supports. If a SIL provider does not sign, write its reason and what we did to reach agreement. Give each party a copy, and give the participant theirs in the format they chose. Set the next review date.

Result
Each party's decision is on the record and each has a copy. A refusal is a record, not a gap.
Record
AGR-SDA-02 Q22; REG-SDA-02 col Y; REG-SDA-02 col Z; REG-SDA-02 col AD; REG-SDA-02 col AH
Time limit
Copies within 2 business days of each decision. Offer again within 28 days of a first refusal; after two refusals, at the 12-month review or when things change (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5. Recorded in: Register col Y, Register col Z, Register col AD, Register col AH.

Step 14

The SDA Manager

Give each SIL provider access and the dwelling's safety information.

Give the keys or codes the participant agreed to. Never restrict a provider the participant chose from entering the dwelling to deliver their supports. The participant decides who enters their bedroom. Walk the provider's first worker through the dwelling. Show the alarms, extinguishers, exits and meeting point, and how to reach our urgent line. Say who maintains and tests each safety feature. Use the latest FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist for the test dates. The SIL provider tells its workers, and any other provider who works there. Write the test dates and the temporary accommodation arrangement.

Result
Each SIL provider can get in, and knows how to get everyone out safely.
Record
AGR-SDA-02 Q27; REG-SDA-02 col AB; REG-SDA-02 col AG
Time limit
Before the SIL provider's first shift in the dwelling (statutory for access: SDA Conditions Rule, section 10(2)(b); SDA Rules 2020, section 37, is the equivalent for registered providers of supports; our standard for the timing)

Carries out: Policy C5, Policy C12. Recorded in: Register col AB, Register col AG.

Day to day

Step 15

Warning. A participant who fears losing their home may stop raising concerns. Silence is not satisfaction.

The Tenancy Officer

Acknowledge the concern.

Anyone can raise a concern: the participant, a housemate, a supporter or a SIL worker. Any worker who hears one passes it to the Tenancy Officer the same day. Write it in the person's own words. Open a concern row in REG-SDA-02 for every concern, whatever it becomes, and sort it with Decision table 3. For an emergency matter, make it safe the same day; for an urgent matter, within 24 hours; phone the urgent line for both. Open a repair in REG-SDA-01 under PRO-SDA-01. If the person is unhappy with a decision, or with something we did or did not do, it is a complaint. Start PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Enter it in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register as "housing or tenancy" and link it in the concern row. Offer an advocate. Give an answer, or a date for one. Tell the person the outcome in their way within 2 business days of closing it. Never treat a person worse for raising a concern.

Result
The person knows who has their concern, what happens next and by when.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BP; REG-SDA-02 col BQ; REG-SDA-02 col BR; REG-SDA-02 col BS; REG-FBK-01 for a complaint; REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register for a repair
Time limit
Acknowledge within 1 business day of the day it was first raised. Answer, or give a date, within 5 business days. Make an emergency matter safe the same day and an urgent one within 24 hours (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8, Policy C14.

Step 16

The SDA Manager

If residents are in conflict and it affects the home or a tenancy, or someone asks us to help:

Help the residents settle the conflict.

A conflict here is a disagreement between people who live in the home. It is not a conflict of interest. The SIL provider and its workers respond first on shift and record it on FRM-SIL-04 Co-Tenant Conflict Record. We join when it affects the dwelling, a shared space, a house rule or a tenancy, or when a resident or the SIL provider asks. Meet each person affected alone, with an advocate or supporter if they want one. Ask what happened from their side, how safe they feel, and what they want. Agree a short written plan with each person: actions, owners and dates. Use mediation only if everyone agrees and nobody is afraid. Never move anyone, change a room or limit access to a shared area to settle it. Where anyone is hurt or afraid, go to step 17 as well. Open a home event row.

Result
Each person has been heard and the conflict is settled or has a plan, and nobody has lost their home.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BI; REG-SDA-02 col BJ
Time limit
Meet each person within 5 business days of learning of the conflict. Review the plan at 28 days (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6. Recorded in: Register col BI, Register col BJ.

Step 17

Warning. Locking a person in or out, blocking their way, taking their things or holding them can injure and frighten them. It is a restrictive practice.

The worker who sees it, hears it or is told

If a person is, or may have been, subjected to violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination in or around a dwelling, or is threatened with harm:

Respond to the incident.

Follow WIN-INC-01 Responding to an Incident (frontline), which sets out steps 1 to 7 of PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. Make people safe. Call 000 first if anyone is hurt or in danger. Do not lock, block or hold anyone, and do not take anyone's things. Where a crime may have happened, do not question further and do not clean up. Phone the SDA Manager, or our urgent line after hours, as soon as people are safe. If the concern is about the SDA Manager, phone the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, phone the independent contact for concerns. You can also phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. Nobody may punish you for reporting. Write the incident report before your shift ends.

Result
Nobody is in immediate danger, a manager knows, and a first-hand account exists.
Record
FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form
Time limit
Straight away. The call as soon as people are safe, and the report before your shift ends (our standard). The law says as soon as possible (statutory: Incident Rules, section 19)

Carries out: Policy C7.

Step 18

The SDA Manager

If the SDA Manager is told of harm, or an allegation of harm, in or around a dwelling:

Manage our response to the harm.

Check that PRO-INC-01 has started. The Quality Manager, as the authorised notifier, decides whether it is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission under PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure. Where abuse, neglect or exploitation is alleged, also start PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure and FRM-SGD-01 Allegation Response and Investigation Record. Speak alone with each person affected. Offer an independent advocate. Ask what they want and what would help them feel safe. Tell the SIL provider the same day if the dwelling is unsafe or damaged, and within 1 business day in any other case. Do this with the participant's agreement unless the law or safety requires otherwise. Do not move or limit the person who was harmed. Open a home event row. Keep each person's account on their own file.

Result
Each person affected is supported, the right reports are made, and the record shows what was done.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BI; REG-SDA-02 col BJ; REG-SDA-02 col BL
Time limit
The same day. The Commission is notified within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days (statutory: Incident Rules, sections 20 and 21)

Carries out: Policy C7, Policy C14. Recorded in: Register col BI, Register col BJ, Register col BL.

Step 19

The SDA Manager

Put right the damage and its cause.

Check the dwelling with the participant's agreement. Make safe anything damaged: locks, doors, fittings and alarms. Open a repair in REG-SDA-01. Brief each contractor on the dwelling entry rules before they enter, with the entry and privacy briefing in PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation), as PRO-SDA-01 step 23 does. Do not ask any participant to pay for damage until we know what caused it, we have offered support and step 25 is done. Never claim against a participant who was harmed. Ask the people affected what would stop it happening again. Ideas include lighting, a roster for shared spaces, a house rule agreed with residents, a talk with the SIL provider, or a lock that the affected resident controls on their own bedroom door after the SDA Manager confirms it limits nobody else. Any lock, gate, sensor, alarm or key restriction that would limit a resident's movement or access is not a remedy here: refer it to the behaviour support pathway under PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure first, and fit nothing until an authorised behaviour support plan covers every resident it affects. Enter each change in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date. Tell each person affected what changed.

Result
The dwelling is safe, and something real has changed to prevent a repeat.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BK; REG-SDA-02 col BM
Time limit
Make safe the same day. Open the repair within 1 business day. Agree changes within 10 business days (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C7. Recorded in: Register col BK, Register col BM.

Step 20

Warning. Locking, blocking access, taking belongings or limiting visitors because of a person's behaviour is a restrictive practice. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can allow it.

The SDA Manager

If a participant's behaviour may put their tenancy at risk:

Manage the behaviour through support, not through the tenancy.

Ask the participant what is happening and how they want to be supported. With their agreement, ask their SIL provider and behaviour support practitioner what would help, whether the plan needs review, and whether the behaviour is a disability-related need that a or a plan review could meet. No notice relying on behaviour starts until the practitioner has answered that question. Look at the dwelling and the house rules. A change to either may help. Consider a reasonable adjustment under FRM-SDA-01. Offer an independent advocate. Record each step. If anyone is in danger now, go to step 17. Step 24 may start only when every step here is done, the problem remains, and the law gives a ground. This procedure authorises no restrictive practice.

Result
Behaviour is managed through the participant's supports, and no tenancy action starts without these steps.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AF
Time limit
Start within 2 business days of learning of it (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C9. Recorded in: Register col AF.

Step 21

The SDA Manager, or the person on the urgent line

If a fire, flood, storm, power or water loss or other event makes the dwelling unsafe or unusable, or a disaster warning affects the area:

Keep each participant safe and housed.

Call 000 if anyone is in danger. The SIL workers on shift lead the move, as the arrangement says. Where no SIL worker is there, phone each participant and their emergency contact, and arrange help. Phone each SIL provider's contact. Use each participant's own plan in FRM-SUP-07 Participant Emergency and Disaster Plan and PLN-EDM-01 Emergency and Disaster Management Plan. With each participant's SIL provider and their emergency plan, arrange safe temporary accommodation as soon as possible and within 24 hours, and a place that meets their access and equipment needs (power for equipment, hoist, pressure care, medication storage, continence) as soon as one can be found. The participant must agree to it. Where a participant's life depends on a device, their medical emergency plan applies and the SIL provider and their practitioner decide the clinical steps. Nobody loses their home because the building is damaged. Check the dwelling is safe before anyone returns. Tell the NDIA at step 2 if it may no longer suit SDA. Open a home event row. Write each person's move and return.

Result
Each participant is safe the same day, housed within 24 hours, and keeps their tenancy.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BN; REG-SDA-02 col BI; REG-SDA-02 col BJ
Time limit
Safe the same day. Temporary accommodation as soon as possible and within 24 hours. The NDIA within 5 business days (our standard; statutory for the NDIA: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

Carries out: Policy C12. Recorded in: Register col BN, Register col BI, Register col BJ.

When needs or circumstances change

Step 22

The Tenancy Officer

Record the change in the participant's needs or circumstances.

A change can come from the participant, a supporter, a SIL provider, a worker or a dwelling check. Ask the participant first whether they agree to us telling others. Write what changed in plain words, with no diagnosis. Tell the providers they chose. Ask what they want from the dwelling or from how we manage it. If a change to the dwelling or to how we manage it may help, start FRM-SDA-01 with them. FRM-SDA-01 asks each other resident affected. Tell the participant the outcome within 2 business days of the decision. If the home may not be able to meet their needs, tell the SDA Manager the same day.

Result
The change is agreed, recorded and passed only to the people the participant chose.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BF; REG-SDA-02 col BG; FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling and Adjustment Request
Time limit
Open the row within 2 business days of the report. Pass it on within 2 business days of the participant's agreement (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Recorded in: Register col BF, Register col BG.

Step 23

Warning. Telling a participant their home may not suit them can feel like being sent away. It can leave them afraid for their home.

The SDA Manager

If FRM-SDA-01 decides the need cannot be met in the dwelling, or the participant's circumstances cannot be accommodated even with adjustments:

Tell the participant that the home cannot meet their needs.

The Chief Executive first reviews every adjustment, modification and alternative, and confirms in writing that none can work. Then tell the participant in person, in their way, with an advocate or supporter if they want one. Explain what was tried and why it cannot work. Say that they decide whether and when to move, and that no notice has been given. Ask who else they want told, such as their support coordinator and SIL providers. Tell them the same day. Offer help to find another home: the support coordinator, the NDIA, and other SDA providers. They keep their home while they look. Do not serve a notice on this ground unless the Chief Executive, after a second review with the participant and an advocate, decides that the risk to the participant or others cannot otherwise be managed and the law of [state or territory] provides the ground; only then does step 24 start. If they choose to leave, follow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure and go to step 28.

Result
The participant and the providers they chose know early that another home is needed, and are helped to find one.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BH
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the Chief Executive's confirmation (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11. Recorded in: Register col BH.

Tenancy notices

Step 24

Warning. A notice given for the wrong reason ends a home unfairly, and is payback.

The SDA Manager

If we plan to give a tenancy notice of any kind:

Check the rule and the reason for the notice.

Find the notice rule row for this kind of notice in REG-SDA-02. If there is no row, or it is more than 12 months old, or the law has changed since it was checked, check the law of [state or territory] first, from the dated list in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. You can ask a tenancy advice service or a lawyer. Then enter a new rule row. Write, in this order: the ground the law requires and the evidence that must accompany the notice; the prescribed or approved form; any prerequisite notice; the least notice; how it must be served; who must receive it; the other parties the law requires to be told and by when; and the body that reviews it. Use Decision table 4. Check the reason. It must not be the participant's choice of SIL provider, a refusal to sign an arrangement, a complaint or concern, or a risk they chose. Write who decided and why. For any notice that would end the tenancy, the Chief Executive approves it in writing first. The second approver is never the person who decided. Open a notice row before you serve anything.

Result
The notice is lawful, has a real ground and has been checked by a second person.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AU; REG-SDA-02 col AV; REG-SDA-02 col AW; REG-SDA-02 col AX; REG-SDA-02 col T
Time limit
Before any notice is served. The rule row checked inside the last 12 months and since the law last changed (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C13. Recorded in: Register col AU, Register col AV, Register col AW, Register col AX.

Step 25

The SDA Manager

If the notice would end the tenancy, record a breach, or limit the participant's rights:

Hear the participant before you decide.

Tell the participant in person, in their way, what is proposed and why. Give them at least 5 business days to answer, with an advocate, supporter or tenancy adviser if they want one. Show them what we hold. Ask for their account and what would help. Consider it and write how you did. Change the proposal if the facts change. Tell the participant the decision and the reasons in their way. If someone's safety is at risk now, go to step 17 first. Then record why a hearing was not possible, and give it as soon as it is safe.

Result
The participant has been heard before anything is decided, and the decision rests on what they said.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AY
Time limit
At least 5 business days for the participant to answer (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C13, Policy C14. Recorded in: Register col AY.

Step 26

Warning. A notice that breaks the state rule may be invalid, and leaves the participant unsure whether they must leave.

The Tenancy Officer

Serve the notice as the rule says.

Use the ground, form, method, time, prerequisite notice and recipients in the notice rule row. Give at least the notice the law requires, and any longer period our agreement or our standards promise: at least 90 days for a notice to vacate; the longer of the law and 60 days for a rent change; the longer of the law and 7 days for an inspection entry, 2 business days for a repair the participant asked for, and no notice only in an emergency the law allows. Serve it on the participant, and on their decision maker if there is one. Tell each other party the law requires, by its time limit. With the participant's consent, give a copy to their advocate and SIL provider. Give the participant a copy in the format they chose, and go through it in their way. Cover the date it takes effect, what it means and what they can do. Ask them to say it back. Write the date and time of service, and the date the law treats it as received. For a rent change, also write the new rent in column S.

Result
The notice is valid, and the participant understands it.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AZ; REG-SDA-02 col BA; REG-SDA-02 col S
Time limit
On the date the rule row sets, and never with less notice than the law requires (statutory: tenancy law of [state or territory])

Carries out: Policy C4, Policy C13. Recorded in: Register col AZ, Register col BA.

Step 27

The Tenancy Officer

Tell the participant how to seek a review.

Do this with every notice, and with every decision about their tenancy, a modification or an application. Tell them in their way that they can ask the Chief Executive to look again, and that we answer within 10 business days. Tell them they can complain to us under PRO-FBK-01. They can contact the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. They can ask an independent advocate and get tenancy advice. They can apply to the tribunal or court for [state or territory] within the time in the notice rule row. Offer to help with any of these. Record which they chose. Say that using any of them never puts their home at risk. Where the notice ends the tenancy, offer help to find another home through their support coordinator and, with consent, their SIL providers. If the NDIA must be told, go to step 2.

Result
The participant knows they can seek a review, and how, and is helped to do it.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BB; REG-SDA-02 col BC; REG-SDA-02 col BE
Time limit
With the notice, and within 2 business days of any other decision about the tenancy (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4, Policy C13. Recorded in: Register col BB, Register col BC, Register col BE.

Step 28

The Tenancy Officer

If a participant gives notice, a notice from us takes effect, a participant dies, or the agreement ends by its terms:

End the tenancy.

Accept a participant's notice in any form. Open a notice row for it. Ask once, and without pressure, whether anything we did or did not do is behind it. Write the answer. Offer help with the move, through their support coordinator and, with consent, their SIL providers, under PRO-SUP-04. Do a final inspection with the participant. Return the bond, and any rent paid ahead, as the law of [state or territory] requires. Write any deduction and the reason. Tell the NDIA at step 2. Open a vacancy row at step 1. Where a participant has died, the incident process runs first under PRO-INC-01 and PRO-INC-02. Speak with their family or the person they named before anything in their room is moved.

Result
The tenancy ends fairly, the bond is settled, and the vacancy is on the record.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col W; REG-SDA-02 col U; REG-SDA-02 col BE
Time limit
Final inspection and bond return as the law requires (statutory: tenancy law of [state or territory]). The vacancy row within 1 business day (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11, Policy C13. Recorded in: Register col W, Register col U, Register col BE.

Check and improve

Step 29

The SDA Manager

Review the register.

Each week, read the open vacancy rows. Check the days since the event, the NDIA notices due and any funding limit date within 14 days. Each month, read the whole register. Look for tenancies with no arrangement row, arrangement reviews due within 60 days, and notice rows with no second approval, hearing or review rights. Look at REG-FBK-01 and REG-SDA-01 for each dwelling, for the days to acknowledge and to answer. Check that each incident at a dwelling in REG-INC-01 has a home event row. Check each notice rule row due for checking within 60 days, and enter a new row if the law changed. Give each gap an owner and a due date. Enter each in REG-QMS-01. Enter a review row.

Result
Gaps are found while there is still time to fix them, and each review leaves a dated record.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BO; REG-SDA-02 col AV
Time limit
Every week for vacancies. Every month for the whole register (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C14. Recorded in: Register col BO.

Step 30

The Quality Manager

Report on tenancy management to the Chief Executive and the governing body.

Every 3 months, trace five rows of each record type to their source records. Show the days to tell the NDIA, the days each place stayed vacant, and whether every resident was asked before each offer. Show tenancies with no arrangement, and each decision. Show every notice that ended or limited a tenancy, with its hearing and review rights. Show concerns, conflicts, harm and changes, with the times met and missed. List the trends and the actions. The Chief Executive and the governing body record decisions in their minutes and in REG-QMS-01. Where there is no governing body, send the report to the independent contact for concerns. Every 12 months, also ask a sample of participants and applicants how clear and fair the vacancy and notice process was. Check every notice rule row. Recommend changes to POL-SDA-05 and to this procedure.

Result
The people who govern [Provider name] see how tenancies are managed and decide what to change.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col BO; REG-QMS-01
Time limit
Every 3 months. The wider check every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C14. Recorded in: Register col BO.

6Decision

Decision table 1: how we choose (steps 3, 5 and 8). Every applicant is checked on the same criteria.

No.CriterionWhat we checkHow it counts
1SDA funding and fitThe applicant's plan includes SDA funding. The dwelling has the design category and building type in their plan, or the NDIA has agreed in writing that this dwelling can be funded for them. The place is a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share. The residents after the move do not exceed the enrolled numberMust be met
2NeedsThe dwelling, and the supports that would be in place, can meet the applicant's needs. Ask the applicant and, with consent, their support coordinator or SIL providerMust be met
3The applicant's own wishesWhether they want this home, its location and this household, as far as they know it. Location can mean nearness to family, work or communityWeighs in favour
4The residents' viewsWhat each resident said about living with a new person. A worry about safety is settled under Decision table 2Weighs in favour
5Order of applicationThe date the applicant appliedUsed only between applicants who are equal on criteria 3 and 4

We never choose, or refuse, because of an applicant's age, diagnosis or type of disability alone, race, religion, sex or sexuality. We never choose because of who delivers their other supports, or whether they use our other services. We never choose because of a gift or reward.

Decision table 2: what the resident says (steps 6 and 7).

The resident saysThen
They have no worry, or no viewRecord it. Do not ask again unless the shortlist changes
They want to meet the person firstOffer a meeting at a time that suits both, with a supporter, if the applicant agrees. Record what each says afterwards
They are worried about daily life together, such as noise, routines or shared spacesMeet them at step 7. Ask what would make it work. Pass any workable idea to the applicant before the offer
They do not feel safe with the personDo not offer the place to that applicant until the resident says the worry is settled. Meet them at step 7. Offer the next applicant if it is not settled
Their worry is about who the person is, such as their disability, race, religion, sex, sexuality or age, and not about how they would live togetherMeet them at step 7. Explain that we cannot refuse an applicant for that reason. Ask what worries them in daily life. Offer an advocate. Do not let that view decide the matter
They cannot say, or do not answerAsk again within 5 business days, in another way or through a supporter who knows them. If there is still no answer, record that and go on. Never treat silence as agreement
They ask for an advocate, or ask us to stopStop. Arrange an advocate within 2 business days. Ask again with the advocate present

Decision table 3: what the person raises (step 15).

What the person raisesTreat it asWhat we do

Phone the urgent line. Tell the participant when it will be fixed. Open the repair in REG-SDA-01. If anyone is in danger, go to step 17

A disagreement with a housemateConflictGo to step 16
A concern about a SIL worker, or the support a SIL provider givesNot ours to answerTell the participant it goes to their SIL provider. With their consent, pass it on the same day. Offer help to complain to the NDIS Commission
A concern that someone is being harmed or is at riskIncidentGo to step 17
A fear of losing their home for raising a concernPayback worrySay plainly that raising a concern never costs them their home. Tell the SDA Manager the same day. Offer an advocate

Decision table 4: before any notice (steps 24 and 25).

The notice is aboutBefore you serve it
Entry to the dwellingCheck the entry rule in the notice rule row. Give the longer of what the law requires and 7 days for an inspection, 2 business days for a repair the participant asked for, and no notice only in an emergency the law allows. Ask the participant for a time that suits them. Enter a bedroom only as the participant agrees, or as the rule allows and the SDA Manager approves. Skip step 25
A change in rentCheck the notice period in the rule row and in AGR-SDA-01, and give the longest of the law, the agreement and 60 days. Check the rent limit as in step 11. Explain how the new rent is worked out. Skip step 25
A breach of the agreement, such as damage or noiseAsk first what is behind it, and offer support. With consent, ask the SIL provider and the behaviour support practitioner whether a disability-related need is behind it and whether a reasonable adjustment or a plan review could meet it; no notice relying on behaviour starts until they have answered. Consider a reasonable adjustment under FRM-SDA-01. Do step 25
Ending the tenancy because the home cannot meet the participant's needsDo not serve a notice. Go to step 23. The Chief Executive reviews every other option first, and a notice follows only if, after a second review with the participant and an advocate, the risk cannot otherwise be managed and the law of [state or territory] provides the ground
Ending the tenancy for another reason the law allows, such as the owner sellingThe Chief Executive approves it. Check the ground, the evidence, the prescribed form, any prerequisite notice and the third parties to be told in the rule row. Give at least 90 days. Do step 25. Offer help to find another home at step 27
The participant's own notice to end the tenancyAccept it in any form. Serve nothing. Go to step 28
The reason is the participant's choice of SIL provider, a refusal to sign an arrangement, a complaint or concern, or a risk they choseDo not serve a notice. It is never a ground. Tell the Chief Executive the same day. Treat any threat to do it as payback and an incident

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A participant refuses to take part in the consultation, the arrangement or a hearingRespect it and record their words. Their tenancy and supports do not change. Offer again once within 28 days, with a different person, time or place, or through an advocate. After two refusals, record their standing answer and ask again only at the 12-month review or when things change. With consent, ask people who know them well
A SIL provider will not sign, or does not answer within 10 business daysRecord the reason or the silence at step 13. Offer again every 28 days. Tell the participant plainly. Their tenancy and supports continue. Tell the Chief Executive after 2 attempts without an answer
Nobody is sure who decides for a participant, or family and the participant disagreeDo not go on the family's word. The SDA Manager reads any order or instrument and records what it covers. The participant still takes part, and an advocate is offered
The participant's FRM-RGT-01 is missing or more than 12 months oldUpdate it with the participant first. Do not send documents until you know the format they want
An interpreter or communication partner is not availableMove the meeting. Do not decide anything with the participant without them. Urgent safety matters go ahead at once
The vacancy follows a deathDo steps 1 and 2 at once, because the limits run. Speak with the family or the person the participant named, and tell the housemates yourself, in their way, before the notice goes up. The Quality Manager, as the authorised notifier, tells the NDIS Commission under PRO-INC-02
A funding limit date is within 14 days and the place is not filledTell the Chief Executive the same day. Widen the advertising and check the criteria. Never lower the bar, press a resident or skip step 6
A time limit in this procedure will be missedTell the person concerned before it passes. Give the reason and the new date, and write both in column J of the register row. The 5 business day limit to the NDIA cannot be extended: notify late rather than never, tell the Chief Executive the same day, and enter it in REG-QMS-01
The Tenancy Officer or SDA Manager is awayThe delegate named in REG-GOV-01 acts. A statutory time limit never waits for a return
The concern is about the SDA Manager, or another managerTake it to the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, take it to the independent contact for concerns. You can always phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. A person never decides, approves or closes a matter about themselves
The notice rule for [state or territory] is missing or unclearDo not serve the notice. Check the law, or ask a tenancy advice service or a lawyer, and enter a rule row. Where safety cannot wait, step 17 comes first, and you get legal advice the same day
A notice was served late, to the wrong person or in the wrong formTell the Chief Executive the same day. Do not rely on it. Tell the participant in plain words, withdraw it in writing, and serve it again correctly if it is still needed. Record it in column BE
A participant says they fear losing their home for raising somethingTell the Chief Executive the same day. Treat any threat to their home as an incident under PRO-INC-01. Offer an advocate
A SIL provider stops supporting a participant suddenlyAsk the participant what they want. With consent, tell their support coordinator the same day. Their home is unchanged. Open a new arrangement row when a new provider starts
Personal information is shared without consent, or sent to the wrong personTell the SDA Manager the same day. Start PRO-INF-02 Privacy and Data Breach Response Procedure
The participant's needs exceed the dwelling's design category or functionality, and no modification can workGo to step 23. Tell the NDIA at step 2 if the design category or suitability changes
An arrangement is out of date, or a contact named in it has leftReview it within 10 business days at step 12. Until then the SDA Manager is our contact. Ask each SIL provider for its new contact the same day
An applicant or a resident says the process was unfairTreat it as a complaint under PRO-FBK-01. The Chief Executive gives another look within 10 business days. Never let it count against them
The system is downUse paper. Phone calls and statutory time limits still apply. Enter the rows within 2 business days of the system coming back

8Done means

A vacancy is finished when all of these are true:

  • the NDIA was told in writing within 5 business days of the event
  • every resident was asked before any offer, and each worry was settled, or the place was not offered to that applicant
  • the place was offered on stated reasons, and every other applicant was told the result and how to challenge it
  • the move-in checks were confirmed, and the place is filled or a new advertising round is open.

An arrangement is finished when all of these are true:

  • each matter has a party responsible, a role, a contact and a response time
  • each party's decision is recorded, in the participant's words for the participant
  • each party has a copy, and the next review date is set.

A change in a participant's needs is finished when all of these are true:

  • the participant was told the outcome in their way
  • the providers they chose were told, within 2 business days of their agreement
  • where the home cannot meet their needs, the participant has been offered help to find another home.

A concern, conflict or harm is finished when all of these are true:

  • the person has been told the outcome in their way
  • the dwelling is safe
  • any change to prevent a repeat is in REG-QMS-01.
  • the concern row shows it was acknowledged within 1 business day and answered within 5

A notice is finished when all of these are true:

  • the rule was checked, and the Chief Executive approved any notice that ends a tenancy
  • the participant was heard, where step 25 applies
  • the notice was served as the law requires
  • the participant was told how to seek a review
  • the NDIA was told, where it had to be.

These records now exist:

  • a row in REG-SDA-02 for each tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, notice, change, home event and concern, and its review rows
  • AGR-SDA-02 for each participant who has a SIL provider
  • the incident report (FRM-INC-01), complaint or repair that any concern led to, linked in column O
  • a dated review row for every weekly, monthly and 3-monthly review.

9Quick card

158 words
  • Call 000 if anyone is hurt or in danger, then phone the SDA Manager or the urgent line (step 17)
  • Tell the NDIA in writing within 5 business days of a vacancy or a notice (step 2)
  • Ask every resident before any offer, and never offer over a resident's safety worry (step 6)
  • Never give notice because of a support choice, a complaint or a refusal to sign (step 24)
  • Check the state rule before every notice, and get the Chief Executive's approval before a notice ends a tenancy (step 24)
  • Hear the participant before you decide anything that ends or limits a tenancy (step 25)
  • Tell the participant how to seek a review with every notice (step 27)
  • Acknowledge a concern about the dwelling within 1 business day; make an emergency one safe the same day and an urgent one within 24 hours (step 15)
  • Never lock, block access or take belongings because of behaviour (step 20)
